sketches: Apply E[F^-] <= E[F] to G = K_n and combine with the paper's theorem that the expected face count of a uniformly random orientable embedding of K_n is ln(n)+O(1); this yields the conjectured ln(n)+O(1) bound for non-orientable random embeddings of K_n.

The same paper establishes that the orientable random embedding of K_n has expected face count ln(n) + O(1); combining this with the general comparison E[F⁻] <= E[F] (Conjecture 9.6) applied to G = K_n gives the non-orientable bound E[F⁻(K_n)] <= ln(n) + O(1), i.e. Conjecture 9.5.

source.name: Non-orientable embedding faces below orientable
source.statement: Let $F^{-}$ be the random variable for the average number of faces in a non-orientable random embedding of some graph $G$. Then $\mathbb{E}[F^{-}] \leq \mathbb{E}[F]$.
source.context: The authors conjecture that the expected face count in a non-orientable random embedding is always at most that of the orientable random embedding, for any graph $G$. The inequality is verified for toy models (including the dipole and chains of triangles joined by cut edges), and an analysis of Random Process A gives the bound $\mathbb{E}[F^{-}] \leq \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}[F] + 1$ for the dipole.

target.name: Non-orientable random embedding faces of Kₙ
target.statement: The expected number of faces in a non-orientable random embedding of the complete graph $K_{n}$ is at most $\ln(n) + O(1)$.
target.context: The authors extend their investigation to non-orientable surfaces, where a random embedding is defined by choosing a random rotation system together with a random signature assigning each edge a sign independently with probability $1/2$. Computer simulations support a logarithmic behaviour analogous to the orientable case.

sketches: Parameter monotonicity: the conjectured bound E[F] <= n/3 + 1 for every simple n-vertex graph is a concrete linear bound, hence immediately gives E[F] = O(n) for uniformly random orientable embeddings.

Both concern the expected number of faces E[F] of a uniformly random orientable embedding of an arbitrary n-vertex simple graph; the explicit bound E[F] <= n/3 + 1 is O(n), so Conjecture 4 of 2202.07746 immediately yields Conjecture 1 of 2103.05036 (which that later paper in fact proved with constant π²/6).
Both concern the expected number of faces of a uniformly random orientable embedding of an arbitrary simple n-vertex graph; the quantitative bound E[F] <= n/3 + 1 immediately gives E[F] = O(n).
The bound E[F] <= n/3 + 1 for every simple n-vertex graph is in particular O(n), the target's statement for uniformly random orientable embeddings.

source.name: Linear face bound in random graph embeddings
source.statement: For any simple graph $G$ of order $n$, $E[F] \leq \frac{1}{3}n + 1$.
source.context: The paper proves $E[F] \leq \frac{\pi^2}{6}n$ for simple graphs (Theorem 8), but no examples approaching this constant are known. A chain of triangles connected by cut edges achieves $E[F] = \frac{1}{3}n+1$, which the authors conjecture is the true optimal bound.

target.name: Linear expected faces in random orientable embeddings
target.statement: For every $n$-vertex simple graph $G$, the expected number of faces when selecting an orientable embedding of $G$ uniformly at random is $O(n)$.
target.context: The authors exhibit a general construction of graph families achieving a linear number of expected faces but were unable to find any family with a superlinear number of expected faces. Results for $d$-regular and $d$-degenerate graphs (Theorem 11 and Corollary 12) are presented as supporting evidence.

sketches: Planar graphs have layered treewidth at most 3 (Dujmovic-Morin-Wood), so if every class of bounded layered treewidth has bounded queue-number, planar graphs have constant queue number. (Both statements are now resolved; the implication was the known route.)
Planar graphs have layered treewidth at most 3 (Dujmovic-Morin-Wood), so if graphs of bounded layered treewidth have bounded queue-number, then planar graphs have constant queue-number.

source.name: Bounded queue-number for layered treewidth graphs
source.statement: It is open whether graphs of bounded layered treewidth have bounded queue-number.
source.context: Dujmović et al. proved that every $n$-vertex graph with layered treewidth $k$ has queue-number $O(k \log n)$. Subsequent to the submission of this paper, improved bounds on queue-number were obtained, but the question of whether a constant bound holds for graphs of bounded layered treewidth remains open.

target.name: Bounded queue number of planar graphs
target.statement: A challenging open problem in the area of queue layouts is to decide whether planar graphs have constant queue number.
target.context: Mentioned in the applications section where the authors note that graphs with bounded queue number form a class with bounded expansion (Dujmović and Wood), so Theorem 1 implies that posets whose cover graphs have bounded queue number have dimension bounded by a function of the queue number and the height. The queue-number problem for planar graphs is cited as independently interesting.

sketches: An n^{2-o(1)} lower bound (no O(n^{2-eps}) algorithm for any eps>0) for map isomorphism is in particular a truly superlinear omega(n polylog n) lower bound for map isomorphism, which is what the subproblem asks to establish (conditionally).

If no O(n^{2-eps}) algorithm exists for map isomorphism for any eps > 0, then in particular no O(n polylog n) algorithm exists (n polylog n = O(n^{1.5})), which is an (even unconditional) truly-superlinear lower bound as sought in 2008.01616__01.

source.name: Quadratic lower bound for map isomorphism
source.statement: There is no $\varepsilon > 0$ for which there is an algorithm for testing isomorphism of maps of unrestricted genus in time $O(n^{2-\varepsilon})$.
source.context: The best known algorithm for the simultaneous conjugation problem runs in time $O(n^2 \log d / \log n + dn \log n)$, yielding an $O(n^2/\log n)$ algorithm for map isomorphism and automorphism problems of unrestricted genus. In complexity theory this is not considered 'truly subquadratic', which motivates the conjecture.

target.name: Superlinear lower bound for map isomorphism
target.statement: An interesting open subproblem is to prove a conditional ``truly superlinear'' lower bound for any of the mentioned problems (map isomorphism, simultaneous conjugation).
target.context: Some progress has been made: the communication complexity of the simultaneous conjugation problem is $\Omega(dn\log n)$ for $d>1$, and under the decision tree model the search version has lower bound $\Omega(n\log n)$. A conditional lower bound ruling out, e.g., $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ algorithms remains open.
